To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the combination of a size polydisperse system with a carefully chosen potential leads to a robust glass-forming system and the swap Monte Carlo method is the most efficient algorithm to study such systems.

(i) the combination of softness, size polydispersity, and non-additivity allows to design novel glass-forming models; (ii) these models are robust against structural ordering and can therefore be efficiently studied by computer simulations; (iii) the performance of the algorithm can be improved by a factor of 10,000 by combining translational displacements with swaps of particle pairs; (iv) the efficiency of the algorithm can further be improved by using a continuous mixture of particle sizes

(i) size polydispersity, (ii) softness, (iii) non-additivity of pair interactions and (iv) swaps of particle pairs are essential ingredients to design computer models with excellent and experimentally relevant glass-forming ability.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel models and algorithms to study the glass transition and the glassy state of matter, with a focus on the development of a new paradigm of glass-forming computer models.
the fundamental question of how glassy systems can be studied efficiently on a computer and we provide the necessary tools to answer this question for the next generation of glass transition studies.
the development of new models and algorithms for the study of the glass transition.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the swap Monte Carlo technique is a powerful and robust tool for the equilibration of a wide variety of glass forming models.
the swap Monte Carlo approach can be successfully applied to all systems studied, and that the efficiency of the method depends on the softness of the interactions.
the combined use of a size polydisperse mixture of particles interacting via a soft potential is a very efficient strategy to design novel computer models with outstanding glass-forming ability.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have found a recipe to create glass-forming models that can be studied efficiently with the swap algorithm.
the swap Monte Carlo is a powerful algorithm for studying supercooled liquids, and that a judicious choice of the potential parameters can lead to models with excellent glass forming ability.
we have found a way to make glass formers that are easy to simulate and that we can use these models to explore the physics of the glass transition.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the combination of a carefully designed model with an efficient Monte-Carlo algorithm is the key to successful computer studies of glass transition.

the combination of a careful choice of the potential and the use of a swap Monte Carlo algorithm can lead to a dramatic increase in the equilibrating timescales and to the development of novel models of supercooled liquids.
the combination of size polydispersion with a soft and non-additive potential can lead to excellent models with a high glass transition temperature and a low fragility.
